sections.title: Scenario
sections.prompt: Why self-host, for whom, and which numbers shape the fleet?
criteria: Converts 1.2M requests a day into average and peak requests per second
Computes monthly input and output tokens
Justifies self-hosting by data control and regulation, not by cost alone
Separates US and EU capacity from the start

sections.title: Single View
sections.prompt: Draw the path from a client to a GPU and to the fallback API.
criteria: Has one gateway enforcing auth, quotas and the data-class rule
Includes admission control and a prefix-aware router as distinct steps
Names a serving engine with continuous batching and multi-LoRA
Includes a model registry for approved, signed versions

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.prompt: What are the platform's inputs, and how do model artifacts arrive safely?
criteria: Registers each use case with entity, data class, priority and quota
Uses safetensors, hash checks, scanning and signing for model artifacts
Serves from an internal mirror rather than a public hub at deploy time

sections.title: Processing
sections.prompt: How many concurrent sequences fit per replica, and how many GPUs does peak need?
criteria: Computes KV bytes per token from layers, KV heads, head dim, K and V, and dtype
Computes concurrent sequences per replica from free HBM
Derives the GPU count from peak prefill and decode tokens per second with a utilization target
Labels per-replica throughput as an assumption to be load-tested

sections.title: Agents
sections.prompt: Is there an agent here, and which levers reduce the fleet?
criteria: States that serving is infrastructure and says what would justify adding an agent
Lists cost levers in order (quantization, model mix, prefix caching, batch shifting) with a monthly saving each
Uses multi-LoRA on one base instead of one deployment per adapter

sections.title: Memory
sections.prompt: What state does the serving layer keep?
criteria: Treats the KV cache as the only state, with prefix caching
Offloads or reuses hot prefixes beyond HBM
Requires stable text first in prompts so prefixes match

sections.title: MCP Tool Servers
sections.prompt: What is the platform's role in tool use?
criteria: Keeps tool execution with the clients, not the serving layer
Offers constrained or guided decoding for structured output
Counts tool definitions against token quotas

sections.title: Endpoints
sections.prompt: What is the API, and how is the TTFT budget spent?
criteria: Gives a TTFT budget by stage under 800 ms at p95
Uses model aliases mapped to pinned versions
Defines priority classes and a batch endpoint
Never sends restricted data to the fallback API

sections.title: Caching
sections.prompt: Beyond the KV cache, what is safe to cache?
criteria: Limits response caching to deterministic requests keyed on model and adapter version
Refuses semantic caching across restricted requests
Keeps frequently used adapters resident

sections.title: Data Stores
sections.prompt: What is stored where, and what does a million tokens cost?
criteria: Computes self-hosted cost per million tokens from fleet cost and tokens served
Compares each model path with a hosted model of similar size at the given prices
States honestly where the hosted API is cheaper
Labels hardware and facility prices as assumed

sections.title: Output
sections.prompt: What do teams, finance and model risk receive?
criteria: Returns token usage including cached tokens on every response
Charges back per use case at an internal rate
Publishes a model card per version

sections.title: Guardrails
sections.prompt: How are residency, data class and model change controlled?
criteria: Enforces data class and region in gateway code
Puts model and adapter changes through evals, model risk approval and a canary
Treats a quantized or re-trained adapter as a new model
Meets EU AI Act deployer duties for the high-risk use case (logs, human oversight)

sections.title: Key Impact
criteria: Tracks use cases unblocked against the 14
Tracks SLO attainment for TTFT and TPOT
Publishes cost per token next to the API comparison

sections.title: Failure Modes
sections.prompt: What happens when capacity is lost?
criteria: Computes load on the surviving data center when one fails
Sheds by priority and data class, and never moves EU data out of the EU
Rolls back a bad model through the registry with weights kept locally

sections.title: Build Order
sections.prompt: How do you bring the fleet up in 9 months?
criteria: Load-tests real traffic before buying the full fleet
Brings regions up one at a time with drills
Ends each phase with a number
